'''Alondes Louis Williams''' (born June 19, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Beijing Ducks]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Triton College|Triton Trojans]], [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma Sooners]], and [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest Demon Deacons]].

==High school career==
Williams played basketball for [[Riverside University High School]] in [[Milwaukee|Milwaukee, Wisconsin]], where he was coached by Tyrone Lewis.<ref name="Bitterman">{{cite news|first=Abby|last=Bitterman|title='He's going to bring the house down': Alondes Williams' dunks bring excitement for Sooners|url=https://www.oklahoman.com/article/5655279/ou-mens-basektball-hes-going-to-bring-the-house-down-alondes-williams-dunks-bring-excitement-for-sooners|work=[[The Oklahoman]]|date=February 18, 2020|access-date=December 16, 2021}}</ref> Williams averaged 12.3 points per game as a senior.<ref>{{cite web|first=Garrett|last=Stepien|title=Oklahoma guard Alondes Williams enters NCAA transfer portal|url=https://247sports.com/Article/Alondes-Williams-transfer-portal-Oklahoma-Sooners-basketball-guard-NCAA-164197959/|website=247Sports.com|date=April 15, 2021|access-date=December 15, 2021}}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman at [[Triton College]], Williams averaged 13.8 points and 6.3 rebounds per game, earning First Team All-[[North Central Community College Conference]] (N4C) accolades.<ref>{{cite web|title=Men's Basketball Standout Williams Signs With Oklahoma|url=https://tritonathletics.com/news/2018/11/15/mens-basketball-standout-williams-signs-with-oklahoma.aspx|website=TritonAthletics.com|publisher=Triton College Athletics|date=November 15, 2018|access-date=December 15, 2021}}</ref> His team won the [[National Junior College Athletic Association]] (NJCAA) Division II title before moving to the NJCAA Division I in the following year.<ref>{{cite web|first=Abby|last=Bitterman|title='Everybody is really rooting for him': After juco success, Alondes Williams is stepping up for OU|url=https://www.oklahoman.com/article/5653435/ou-mens-basketball-everybody-is-really-rooting-for-him-alondes-williams-is-starting-to-get-comfortable-after-transitioning-from-juco-to-sooners|work=[[The Oklahoman]]|date=January 28, 2020|access-date=December 15, 2021}}</ref> In his sophomore season, Williams averaged 17 points, 7.7 rebounds and 5.3 assists per game, and was named N4C Player of the Year. He transferred to [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]] for his junior season, and averaged six points and 1.9 rebounds per game. As a senior, Williams averaged 6.7 points and 2.8 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|first=Les|last=Johns|title=Wake Forest officially announces addition of Oklahoma transfer Alondes Williams|url=https://247sports.com/college/wake-forest/Article/Wake-Forest-officially-announces-addition-of-Oklahoma-transfer-Alondes-Williams--165861616/|website=247sports.com|publisher=Demon Deacon Digest|date=May 28, 2021|access-date=December 15, 2021}}</ref> He opted to use an additional year of eligibility and transferred to [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Ryan|last=Chapman|title=Former Oklahoma Forward Alondes Williams Announces Transfer Destination|url=https://www.si.com/college/oklahoma/mens-basketball/former-oklahoma-forward-alondes-williams-announces-transfer-destination|website=SI.com|publisher=All Sooners|date=May 21, 2021|access-date=December 15, 2021}}</ref> On December 11, 2021, Williams posted the second [[triple-double]] in program history, with 16 points, 14 rebounds and 10 assists in a 79–53 win against [[USC Upstate Spartans men's basketball|USC Upstate]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Ethan|last=Joyce|title=Alondes Williams records second triple-double in program history during Wake Forest win|url=https://journalnow.com/sports/college/wfu/alondes-williams-records-second-triple-double-in-program-history-during-wake-forest-win/article_6c7b574a-5aec-11ec-84f6-8f30f5403cff.html|work=[[Winston-Salem Journal]]|date=December 11, 2021|access-date=December 15, 2021}}</ref> In his next game, three days later, he scored a career-high 36 points in a 77–70 victory over [[VMI Keydets basketball|VMI]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Williams leads Wake Forest in 77-70 comeback win over VMI|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401370061|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=December 14, 2021|access-date=December 15, 2021}}</ref> Williams was named [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|ACC Player of the Year]].<ref name=ACCAwards>{{cite press release|title=ACC Unveils 2021-22 Men's Basketball Awards|url=https://theacc.com/news/2022/3/6/athlete-awards-acc-unveils-2021-22-mens-basketball-awards.aspx|website=TheACC.com|publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]]|date=March 7, 2022|access-date=March 7, 2022}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Brooklyn / Long Island Nets (2022–2023)===
After being undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]], Williams signed a two-way contract with the [[Brooklyn Nets]] on July 4, 2022,<ref>{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Alondes Williams|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2022/07/04/brooklyn-nets-sign-alondes-williams|website=NBA.com|date=July 4, 2022|access-date=July 5, 2022}}</ref> but was waived on January 12, 2023, after appearing in just one regular-season game.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Waive Alondes Williams|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-waive-alondes-williams|website=NBA.com|date=January 12, 2023|access-date=January 14, 2023}}</ref> Six days later, Williams was reacquired by the [[Long Island Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/22-23-nba-g-league-transactions|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 18, 2023}}</ref>

===Miami Heat / Sioux Falls Skyforce (2023–2024)===
On July 24, 2023, Williams signed with the [[Miami Heat]],<ref>{{cite web|title=HEAT MAKE ROSTER MOVES|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-make-roster-moves|website=NBA.com|date=August 11, 2023|access-date=August 12, 2023}}</ref> but was waived on October 14<ref>{{cite web|title=HEAT WAIVE PETERSON AND WILLIAMS|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-waive-peterson-and-williams|website=NBA.com|date=October 14, 2023|access-date=October 15, 2023}}</ref> and sixteen days later, he joined the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Skyforce Announces Training Camp Roster Ahead of 2023-24 Season|url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-announces-training-camp-roster-ahead-of-2023-24-season|website=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=January 28, 2024}}</ref> On February 9, 2024, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Heat<ref>{{cite web|title=HEAT SIGN ALONDES WILLIAMS TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-alondes-williams-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=February 9, 2024|access-date=February 9, 2024}}</ref> and on April 5, he was named the [[NBA G League Most Improved Player Award|NBA G League Most Improved Player]] after averaging 20.3 points on 49.8 percent from the field, 5.3 rebounds. 7.1 assists, 1.3 steals and 0.6 blocks per 37.4 minutes a game in 43 appearances.<ref>{{cite web|title=Skyforce Duo Earns NBA G League End Of Season Awards|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-duo-earns-nba-g-league-end-of-season-awards|website=NBA.com|date=April 5, 2024|access-date=April 5, 2024}}</ref>

On September 30, 2024, Williams signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]],<ref>{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Alondes Williams Signs Camp Deal With Clippers|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/09/alondes-williams-reportedly-joining-clippers.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=September 30, 2024|access-date=October 21, 2024}}</ref> but was waived on October 19.<ref>{{cite web|first=Arthur|last=Hill|title=Clippers Waive Elijah Harkless, Alondes Williams, Braxton Key|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/10/clippers-waive-elijah-harkless-alondes-williams-braxton-key.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 21, 2024}}</ref>

===Detroit Pistons / Motor City Cruise (2024–2025)===
On October 22, 2024, Williams signed a two-way contract with the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|title=DETROIT PISTONS SIGN ALONDES WILLIAMS TO A TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-alondes-williams-to-a-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=October 22, 2024|access-date=October 22, 2024}}</ref> However, he was waived on January 6, 2025.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Pistons PR|title=The @DetroitPistons announced today that the team has signed Ron Harper Jr. and Tolu Smith to two-way contracts. Per team policy, terms of the agreement were not disclosed. In a related move, the Pistons waived forward Cole Swider and guard Alondes Williams.|number=1876388325537497524|user=Pistons_PR|date=January 6, 2025|access-date=January 7, 2025}}</ref>

===Return to Sioux Falls (2025)===
On January 12, 2025, Williams returned to the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Skyforce Reacquires Alondes Williams|url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-reacquires-alondes-williams|website=NBA.com|date=January 12, 2025|access-date=January 12, 2025}}</ref>

=== Washington Wizards / Capital City Go-Go (2025–2026)===
On October 13, 2025, Williams signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wizards add Kadary Richmond and Alondes Williams |url=https://www.talkbasket.net/204130-wizards-add-kadary-richmond-and-alondes-williams |website=TalkBasket.net |date=October 13, 2025 |access-date=October 14, 2025}}</ref> On February 16, 2026, he signed a 10-day contract with the Wizards.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Washington Signs Alondes Williams To 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/washingtonsignsalondes-williamsto-10-day-contract|access-date=March 31, 2026|website=nba.com|language=en}}</ref> On February 20, Williams recorded a career-high 25 points and 10 rebounds in a 131-118 victory over the [[2025–26 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Alondes Williams has career night in the Wizards' victory over the Pacers|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/alondes-williams-career-night-wizards-024244109.html|access-date=February 23, 2026|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}}</ref>

In July 2026, Williams joined the [[Boston Celtics]] for the [[2026 NBA Summer League]].<ref>https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press-release-20260708-celtics-announce-2026-nba-summer-league-roster-and-schedule</ref>
